purpose: Rule-source register for PlayAtlas. Sources are research references; PlayAtlas tutorials and code are rewritten independently.

methodology.history_policy: A source that documents a game does not by itself prove a unique origin, oldest status, or single canonical regional form.
methodology.variant_policy: When sources disagree, the catalog names one default ruleset and records the disagreement instead of silently merging rules.

sources.title: Snake (video game)
sources.use: Mechanic orientation only; no copied art, text or code.

sources.title: Breakout (video game)
sources.use: Mechanic orientation only; PlayAtlas uses original visuals and levels.

sources.title: Minesweeper (video game)
sources.use: Terminology and common mechanics; first-click-safe/no-guess policy must be stated separately.

sources.title: Nikoli Sudoku rules
sources.use: Rows, columns and 3x3 blocks each contain 1-9. Nikoli page also identifies Number Place history; do not copy trademarked branding.

sources.title: Original 2048 project repository
sources.use: Mechanic/reference only; repository license and attribution must be checked before any code reuse. PlayAtlas implementation is independent.

sources.title: Sokoban official site
sources.use: Confirms original game identity and trademark notice; do not copy protected levels, rabbit mark or branding.

sources.title: 15 puzzle
sources.use: Classic 4x4 objective and solvability/parity reference.

sources.title: Shisen-Sho
sources.use: Two-turn path rule and dead-board semantics; page itself requests more citations, so treat as a starting point and verify against KDE handbook or another specialist source.

sources.title: International Rules of Gomoku (RIF)
sources.use: 15x15 board, swap-2 opening, exactly-five condition and draw language. Do not call a freestyle implementation RIF-compliant.

sources.title: Gomoku overview and freestyle variant
sources.use: Freestyle variant is described as unrestricted placement with five-or-more winning. Used only to document the sample module's chosen adaptation; not an official federation rulebook.

sources.title: What is Othello?
sources.use: World Othello Federation public introduction; exact tournament edge cases still need a rulebook review.

sources.title: World Xiangqi Rules
sources.use: Primary source for WXF movement, check, repetition and chase policy.

sources.title: Complete Implementation of WXF Chinese Chess Rules
sources.use: Secondary technical cross-check for repetition adjudication; not a replacement for the WXF rulebook.

sources.title: Connect 4 Game Instructions
sources.use: Classic 7x6 four-in-a-row setup; Hasbro trademarks are not used in PlayAtlas art or copy.

sources.title: Dots and boxes
sources.use: Standard edge-drawing, box completion and extra-turn mechanics; no single federation ruleset claimed.

sources.title: WCDF Rules of Checkers / English Draughts
sources.use: English draughts only: compulsory capture, non-flying kings and WCDF draw policy. Do not import international 10x10 maximum-capture rules.

sources.title: Nine Men's Morris rules
sources.use: Placement, movement, mills, removal and flying reference; variant/draw policy still requires a named lock.

sources.title: FIDE Laws of Chess effective 1 January 2023
sources.use: Primary source for legal moves, checkmate, stalemate, castling, en passant, promotion and draw rules.

sources.title: Klondike Solitaire rules
sources.use: Community reference only; draw-one/draw-three and recycle limits are variants and must be shown.

sources.title: Spider Solitaire rules
sources.use: Two-deck and suit-run mechanics reference; no publisher assets or text are bundled.

sources.title: FreeCell rules
sources.use: All-cards-face-up, free-cell and legal-move reference; implementation remains independent.

sources.title: Pyramid Solitaire rules
sources.use: Pairs-to-13 and exposed-card rules; stock recycle convention must be locked explicitly because sources vary.

sources.title: Hearts card-game rules
sources.use: American Hearts reference including pass cycle, follow-suit, penalty scoring and shoot-the-moon.

sources.title: Gin Rummy card-game rules
sources.use: Two-player ten-card Gin Rummy deal, knock, gin and scoring reference.

sources.title: Go Fish card-game rules
sources.use: Ask-for-rank, draw and quartet completion reference; end conditions must be fixed in the game card.

sources.title: Crazy Eights card-game rules
sources.use: Rank/suit matching and eight-wild reference; draw and scoring house rules are recorded as variants.

sources.title: Oware Abapa rules
sources.use: Abapa sowing, feeding and capture reference; source is not an official national federation rulebook.

sources.title: Oware rules (Oware Game)
sources.use: Independent cross-check of Abapa terminology and end conditions; differences must be recorded rather than merged silently.

sources.title: Sungka evidence record
sources.use: Ludii Digital Ludeme Project evidence record citing Bernardo (1937), including 2x7 board, sowing, capture and refill description.

sources.title: Philippine National Museum games collection
sources.use: Cultural context and equipment reference; museum text is not copied into tutorials.

sources.title: Yut/Nyout official rulebook
sources.use: Structured rulebook explicitly identifies its Korean Cultural Heritage Foundation and Pagat cross-checks; verify citations before claiming official status.

sources.title: Korea.net: traditional board game Yutnori
sources.use: Cultural context and broad stick/race description; detailed branch/stacking rules require the selected rulebook.

sources.title: Baghchal rules
sources.use: 4-tiger/20-goat setup and movement reference; source is not a government cultural authority.

sources.title: Ludii / Digital Ludeme Project portal
sources.use: Use as a research entry point and cross-check; do not embed Ludii code/database in PlayAtlas without separate license review.

sources.title: Scopa card-game rules
sources.use: Standard Scopa capture, sweeps, primiera and round scoring reference; Scopone is a separate variant.

sources.title: Briscola card-game rules
sources.use: Standard two-player Briscola trump, trick and point-order reference.

sources.title: Te Ara: Traditional Māori games
sources.use: Cultural context and explicit note that evidence/rules history can be debated; no single-origin claim.

sources.title: NRICH Mū Tōrere
sources.use: Playable reconstruction and teaching reference; selected center-entry rule must be named as a reconstruction.

sources.title: Fanorona
sources.use: Fanoron-Sivy board, approach/withdrawal and compulsory capture overview; verify against a primary Malagasy or Ludii source before release.

sources.title: Ludii General Game System
sources.use: Candidate database for a rule record; exact Fanorona record and license must be located before using as a release source.

sources.title: International Carrom Federation Laws of Carrom (PDF mirror)
sources.use: ICF equipment, queen, fouls and scoring reference; mirror provenance should be rechecked against ICF before shipping.

sources.title: International Carrom Federation
sources.use: Confirms ICF role in compiling/enforcing rules; use for attribution and current-rulebook lookup.

sources.title: USAA Official Rules of Air Hockey (public mirror)
sources.use: First-to-seven, serve and foul reference; verify against current USAA rule publication before launch.

sources.title: USBC Playing Rules
sources.use: Current ten-pin rules and scoring authority; exact version must be frozen in the game rules card at implementation time.

sources.title: World Minigolf Sport Federation rules index
sources.use: Official federation entry point; locate and freeze the exact rulebook revision before claiming WMF compliance.

sources.title: WMF event document referencing worldwide international sport rules
sources.use: Confirms WMF worldwide rules are used for the cited event; PlayAtlas holes remain an explicitly labeled digital adaptation.
